title: The Facade of the Fate Writer
next_chapter_hook: The phantom of the Fate Writer trembled slightly, those eyes that had seen through the ages suddenly narrowed: 'It seems you are more interesting than I anticipated—and more valuable.'

text.content: The ancient will's whisper exploded in Chen Ji's Mental Sea like rolling thunder, each word carrying the weight and vicissitudes of countless ages. 'Our bloodline will bring this ancient chess game to its end.' These words seared into his soul's depths, intertwining with the faint glow of the Tianji Record Fragment. Chen Ji felt a burning sensation in his chest, as if something long dormant was awakening. He unconsciously clenched his fists, knuckles whitening, though his expression remained characteristically calm. Only in the depths of his eyes did a ripple pass that even he could barely察觉—a thought about Chen Nian. His sister, far away in the Holy Sect, did she feel the same summons?

Su Qingyao's voice pulled Chen Ji back to reality. He turned to look at this Inner Disciple Senior Fellow beside him, noting her slightly furrowed brow and those usually cold eyes that now showed rare traces of worry. Under the moonlight, her white Inner Disciple robe fluttered in the mountain wind, three thousand strands of blue-black hair dancing gently. Even in this tense moment, she maintained her aloof, formidable demeanor, but Chen Ji knew it was merely her protective shell. Su Qingyao was the only one who had noticed something amiss with him—three times she'd approached the truth, three times he'd deftly deflected her.

Chen Ji spoke flatly, his tone as still as dead water. He would never let anyone see his vulnerabilities, not even Su Qingyao. Yet just then, a sudden change occurred—the Tianji Record Fragment began to vibrate violently, and an unfamiliar line of ancient text appeared on the yellowed surface. 'The Fate Writer is about to arrive.' These words flashed before Chen Ji's eyes, followed by an unprecedented pressure descending from above, as if invisible hands were manipulating the threads of fate.

dialogue.content: No need to be nervous. I've come merely to have a word with you.

text.content: This voice didn't enter through his ears, but resounded directly within Chen Ji's soul. At the same time, a phantom slowly materialized before the two of them. The visitor was an elderly man with silver-white hair, wearing a plain white robe, his face as serene as an ancient well, as if he had witnessed all the world's joys and sorrows. His eyes were deep as an abyss, his pupils seemingly reflecting the birth and death of countless stars, as if time's passage had lost all meaning before him. This was the Fate Writer—the legendary fourth-pole existence that supposedly stood above the Three Sects.

Su Qingyao instantly drew her sword, its light cold and sharp as autumn water. Her reaction was faster than Chen Ji had anticipated—this Inner Disciple Senior Fellow clearly had well-deserved reputation. 'Who are you!' Her voice was cold and biting as frost, sword tip pointing directly at the phantom. However, the white-robed elder merely glanced at her with raised eyes, and Su Qingyao staggered backward several steps as if struck by lightning, shock clearly visible on her face for the first time. One glance alone rendered the Foundation Building late-stage Inner Disciple Senior Fellow powerless—this was merely the tip of the iceberg regarding fourth-pole strength.

Chen Ji's voice was not loud, yet carried undeniable authority. He stepped forward, shielding Su Qingyao behind him, facing that phantom that seemed able to see through everything, his expression still coldly indifferent as usual. 'Junior Chen Ji pays respects to the senior.' He clasped his hands in a formal salute, respectful yet neither servile nor overbearing. Even knowing the opponent could overturn seas and move mountains as a fourth-pole existence, he would not show a trace of timidity. Beneath that meek exterior lay a ruthless mind that calculated without error.

dialogue.content: Indeed a Tianqing Sect servant disciple, just as I anticipated.

text.content: The Fate Writer nodded slightly, a hint of appreciation flickering in his eyes. His gaze seemed able to pierce through all Chen Ji's disguises, seeing the sharp edge hidden beneath that calm mask. 'Holder of the Tianji Record, in ten thousand ages, you are the second person to make me appear in person.' At these words, Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. The second—then who was the first? The true origins of the Tianji Record were far more complex than he'd imagined. And this elder before him clearly knew many secrets he had yet to uncover.

choice.prompt: Faced with this mysterious existence that surpassed the Three Sects, Chen Ji needed to make his first judgment—

choices.description: Since the other party took the initiative to appear, they must have ulterior motives. Let's hear the terms first, then decide.
choices.visible_reward: Gain intelligence on the fourth-pole forces
choices.risk_hint: Risk falling into the other party's chess game
choices.process_label: 陈机微微颔首，表示愿意聆听。

text.content: The Fate Writer seemed quite satisfied with his response, the phantom nodding slightly: 'A wise choice.' The white-robed elder's voice carried a note of approval, 'You should know, the Three Sects are merely puppets on stage. The true chess game has always unfolded in deeper places.'

choices.description: Don't rush to take a stance; first gauge how deep their waters are. Know yourself and your enemy, and you will be invincible in every battle.
choices.visible_reward: Understand the true strength of the fourth pole
choices.risk_hint: The other party may lose patience
choices.process_label: 陈机眯起眼睛，似笑非笑地看着对方。

text.content: Chen Ji did not retreat; instead, he met that gaze that had seen through ages, speaking calmly: 'Since the senior knows of the Tianji Record, surely you also know what it signifies. May I inquire what relationship the senior has with the Heavenly Secrets Eye?' This question directly struck the core. A hint of surprise flickered in the Fate Writer's eyes, then transformed into an amused smile. 'Interesting, you actually already know of the Heavenly Secrets Eye's existence.'

choices.description: Regardless of who you are, no one under heaven or earth can make decisions for him. He has his own path to walk.
choices.process_label: 陈机嘴角勾起一抹冷笑。

text.content: Yet Chen Ji's next words caused the Fate Writer's expression to change for the first time. 'The senior's kindness, the junior is grateful for. However—' He raised his head, and those usually calm eyes now revealed a sharp brilliance that seemed to look down upon all beneath heaven, 'The junior's path has never needed others to point the way.'

The Fate Writer fell silent for a moment, the surrounding air seeming to freeze. Su Qingyao behind Chen Ji gripped her sword hilt tightly, knuckles white; she could feel the phantom's aura pressuring down bit by bit. Yet Chen Ji remained motionless, simply staring calmly at his opponent. After a片刻, the white-robed elder suddenly laughed—laughter old yet hearty, echoing through the night sky. 'Ha ha ha! Good! Good! Good!' He said three 'goods' in succession, eyes blazing with brilliant light, 'In ten thousand years, you are the first person to dare speak to me this way.'

dialogue.content: It seems I truly underestimated you.

text.content: Chen Ji did not respond, merely watching the other party quietly. The Fate Writer's phantom paced slowly, those eyes that had seen through ages打量ing Chen Ji repeatedly, as if examining a priceless treasure. 'The Tianji Record chose you for a reason.' He spoke slowly, voice deep, 'You are a chess player, not a chess piece. This is more important than anything.' He paused, then shifted topics, 'But you should also be clear—the more complete the Tianji Record becomes, the stronger fate's inevitable backlash.' These words poured cold water over Chen Ji's heart.

dialogue.content: I can help you. At least in the initial stages.

text.content: Chen Ji's question was brief and direct. He knew only too well—no free lunches in the world. Since the Fate Writer represented an independent fourth-party force willing to help, his ambitions must be considerable. However, the white-robed elder's answer caught him by surprise. 'Conditions?' The Fate Writer chuckled lightly, 'My condition is very simple—when one day you stand at the pinnacle of the chess game and look back at your journey, remember that an old man once reminded you: You belong to no chess game, not even mine.'

These words made Chen Ji's heart jolt. Belong to no chess game—including the Fate Writer's? That was too contradictory. If the other party didn't want to control him, why appear at all? Why offer help? Unless... their goal was not in competition with him, but some deeper level of connection. Just as Chen Ji pondered, the Fate Writer's phantom began to dissipate. 'That's enough for today.' His voice faded into the distance, 'Remember, time is running out. The Heavenly Secrets Eye's gaze is closer than you imagine.'

choice.prompt: As the Fate Writer's form was about to dissipate completely, Chen Ji had to make a decision—

choices.description: Since the other party refuses to be explicit, then first accept this kindness and observe secretly. After all, one more friend is better than one more enemy.
choices.visible_reward: Gain covert support from fourth-pole forces
choices.risk_hint: Risk being used without knowing it

dialogue.content: The junior will remember the senior's words.

text.content: Before the phantom fully vanished, the Fate Writer's voice rang out one last time: 'You will need this.' An ancient jade slip appeared before Chen Ji out of thin air, covered in ancient patterns similar to the Tianji Record. This was... some kind of inheritance or guidance? Chen Ji did not immediately reach for it, waiting until that aura had completely disappeared before slowly picking up the jade slip. He could sense the power contained within—power enough to change the battlefield.

choices.description: Since the other party mentioned the Heavenly Secrets Eye, it means they know more inside information. The thicker the fog, the more it indicates secrets behind this that can overturn one's understanding.
choices.risk_hint: The other party may refuse to speak further
choices.process_label: 陈机眼中精光一闪，猛然开口。

dialogue.content: Since the senior mentioned the Heavenly Secrets Eye, surely you know its origins. The junior ventures to ask the senior to enlighten us!

text.content: The largely dissipated phantom paused slightly, those deep eyes giving Chen Ji one final look. 'Your sister, Chen Nian—' Just these five words caused Chen Ji's pupils to contract sharply, his heart feeling as if gripped by an invisible hand. 'She is not merely a key.' The Fate Writer's voice grew increasingly distant, 'Ask the one on the first page of the Tianji Record; it will tell you everything.' The words fell, the phantom completely dissipated, as if it had never existed.

Night wind brushed across the mountain peak, dispersing the last traces of strange aura. Su Qingyao sheathed her sword and walked to Chen Ji's side, gazing at him with complex eyes. Everything that had just transpired was too great a shock for her. Fourth-pole forces, the Heavenly Secrets Eye, Chen Nian... these names, strung together, outlined a grand chess game far beyond her imagination. And this servant disciple labeled as 'waste material' was actually a key figure in this game of cosmic proportions. 'Chen Ji,' her voice somewhat hoarse, 'who... exactly are you?'

dialogue.content: A person who wants to protect his family.

text.content: Chen Ji turned around, looking into those eyes filled with complex emotions. He did not evade, nor did he continue to conceal—at least, not completely. Moonlight fell upon his face, and on that usually calm visage, a rare hint of gentleness now appeared. 'Qingyao,' he called softly, his voice carrying an unprecedented seriousness, 'There are things I still cannot tell you now. But I promise—when the time is right, I will personally tell you everything.' He paused, the corners of his mouth lifting slightly, 'Until then, can you... continue to keep this secret for me?'

Su Qingyao's response was soft, so soft it was nearly scattered by the mountain wind. But Chen Ji heard it. He saw something in those usually cold eyes that was quietly changing. From investigator to protector—Su Qingyao's role transformation happened faster than he'd anticipated. This might have been his deliberate doing, or perhaps... the arrangement of fate. Either way, after tonight, their relationship had already changed. And the riddle left behind by the Fate Writer—Chen Nian's secret—had planted an even deeper obsession in his heart.

Just then, the jade slip in Chen Ji's hand suddenly grew warm. He looked down to see rows of faint text appearing on the ancient surface—the final message left by the Fate Writer: 'The Heavenly Secrets Eye's gaze is closer than you imagine.' Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, gazing into the depths of the night sky. He had a intuition—something was watching him from the shadows. An existence beyond the Three Sects, beyond the fourth pole—the true chess player behind the ancient game. The Heavenly Secrets Eye... was it finally about to reveal its true form?
